scope: src/main.js lines 11876-12947 — spatial wall index, nav grid + A*, cover-edge/slot baking, Squad class, EnemyManager (spawnByZone, repair, separation, boss-phase interpreter, awareness, update/muzzle-flash). Cross-checked cover-graph.js impls.

findings.title: Boss-spawned adds mis-tagged to zone 2 when boss is in zone 0 (`||` swallows zoneId 0)
findings.description: In EnemyManager._runBossPhase addSpawn, the spawn-clearance opts use the correct `Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2` (line 12758), but the very next line tags the new enemy with `newE.zoneId=boss.zoneId||2`. Because `0||2===2`, a boss whose zoneId is 0 (front zone) produces adds tagged zoneId 2 (back). Those adds are then counted in the wrong zone by per-zone systems (squad grouping, awareness radius gating uses zoneId, encounter/cover slot zone filters), and the room-clear gate becomes inconsistent with where the enemies physically are.
findings.evidence:
line 12758: zoneId:Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2  // correct
line 12763: newE.zoneId=boss.zoneId||2;  // wrong: zoneId 0 -> 2
findings.fix: Change line 12763 to `newE.zoneId=Number.isFinite(boss.zoneId)?boss.zoneId:2;` (mirror the opts on line 12758). Surgical one-token change, no save-compat impact.
findings.risk: None to save format. Only affects which zone freshly boss-spawned adds are accounted to; corrects a desync. Bosses are usually placed in zone 2 so today the bug is latent, but it activates for any zone-0/zone-1 boss encounter.

findings.title: Dead duplicate peek-slot selector with a type-mismatch bug (`s.claimedBy !== agentX`)
findings.description: cover-graph.js getBestPeekSlot (wrapped by `_getBestPeekSlot` at main.js line 12052) compares `s.claimedBy` (an enemy object) against `agentX` (a number coordinate) at line 251 `if (s.claimedBy && s.claimedBy !== agentX) continue;`. Since claimedBy is never a number, the condition is always true for any claimed slot, so every claimed slot is always skipped — the function can never reuse the agent's own slot. This is a buggy DUPLICATE of the LIVE selector Enemy._bestPeekSlot (main.js ~line 10826) which correctly does `if(s.claimedBy&&s.claimedBy!==this)continue;`. `_getBestPeekSlot`/`getBestPeekSlot` is never called from anywhere in src/ (only the wrapper definition + import alias exist), so it is dead code. The live path is unaffected.
findings.evidence: main.js: `_getBestPeekSlot` defined at 12052-12054, zero call sites (grep `_getBestPeekSlot(` matches only the definition). cover-graph.js line 251: `if (s.claimedBy && s.claimedBy !== agentX) continue;` — claimedBy is an Enemy object, agentX is a float.
findings.fix: Either delete the dead `_getBestPeekSlot` wrapper + its import alias and the cover-graph export, or, if it is meant to be revived, change its signature to take the agent object and fix line 251 to `s.claimedBy !== agent`. Lowest-risk: remove the dead wrapper to prevent a future caller hitting the broken comparison.
findings.risk: Removing is safe (no callers). Reviving requires a signature change at all (zero) call sites. No runtime behavior changes today.

findings.title: `_cellWallsAt` spatial-index point accessor is never called
findings.description: `_cellWallsAt(idx,x,z)` is defined as the point-query accessor for the wall spatial index, but no code uses it. The actual hot-path consumers (main.js 10352-10363, 10391, 25047) index `_idx.cells[cellId]` inline instead of calling this helper. Harmless but dead, and a maintenance trap: the inline consumers and this helper compute the cell id with slightly different rounding (`((x-xMin)/cs)|0` here vs the inline DDA in canSee), so a future caller switching to this helper could silently diverge.
findings.evidence: grep `_cellWallsAt` across src/ matches only the definition at line 11918. Hot paths instead do e.g. line 10360 `_cellWalls=_idx.cells[cellId];`.
findings.fix: Delete `_cellWallsAt` (lines 11918-11924), or route the inline `_idx.cells[...]` lookups through it for a single source of truth. Prefer deletion since the inline DDA traversal is the perf-tuned path.
findings.risk: Deletion is safe (no callers). No build/probe impact.

findings.title: Boss `peekBurst` comment says 'temporarily' but peekRate is buffed permanently (no restore)
findings.description: The peekBurst boss command stores `boss._peekRateOrig` and multiplies `boss.peekRate` by cmd.mul, with the comment 'Bump peek rate temporarily for the duration of the phase'. There is no timer or revert that restores peekRate after the phase, and boss phases fire exactly once (`ph.fired`). So the buff is permanent, contradicting the comment. Functionally a permanent enrage is probably fine, but the stored `_peekRateOrig` is written and never read back, i.e. an effect set up for restoration that never happens.
findings.evidence: line 12775-12777: `boss._peekRateOrig=boss._peekRateOrig||boss.peekRate; boss.peekRate=boss._peekRateOrig*(cmd.mul||2.0);` — no code reads `_peekRateOrig` to restore, and the comment claims it is temporary.
findings.fix: Either drop the misleading 'temporarily' from the comment (accept permanent enrage), or actually make it temporary by recording an expiry (e.g. `boss._peekRateRestoreAt=performance.now()+ph.durMs`) and restoring `boss.peekRate=boss._peekRateOrig` in EnemyManager.update when that time passes. Documentation-vs-code mismatch only; no crash.
findings.risk: Low. If made temporary, verify no other code already restores peekRate; if left permanent, just a comment edit.

findings.title: Enemy muzzle-flash hidden via wall-clock setTimeout that can fire after the enemy is removed/disposed
findings.description: Each enemy shot schedules `setTimeout(()=>{ ... e.muzzleFlashH.material.opacity=0; ... },55)` to hide the flash. (1) Dead enemies are filtered+removed in the same update at line 12935 (`forEach(e=>e.remove())`), and remove() disposes the muzzle-flash materials (traverse at 11866-11870). A pending 55ms timeout then touches a disposed material — harmless (no throw) but operates on a freed object and the closure retains the Enemy+group, briefly preventing GC. (2) The flash is set to full opacity for a fixed wall-clock 55ms with NO per-frame decay, so at high FPS it pops on/off as a hard step (less premium) and at very low FPS it may render for several frames or be missed entirely. The flash duration is decoupled from the frame loop unlike the rest of the VFX (G.trails are timer-driven in the loop).
findings.evidence: line 12919: `setTimeout(()=>{ if(e.muzzleFlashH){e.muzzleFlashH.material.opacity=0;e.muzzleFlashH.visible=false;} ... },55);` plus remove() disposing materials at 11866-11870 and the dead-enemy filter+remove at 12935 in the same update tick.
findings.fix: Drive the flash fade in the frame loop instead of setTimeout: stamp `e._muzzleFlashUntil=performance.now()+55` on fire and, in EnemyManager.update (or Enemy.update), lerp opacity toward 0 / set invisible once `now>e._muzzleFlashUntil`, guarding `if(!e.dead && e.muzzleFlashH && e.muzzleFlashH.material)`. This removes the dangling timeout, ties the flash to render frames, and lets you add a 1-2 frame decay for a punchier AAA flash.
findings.risk: Low. Must guard against the disposed material; keep the existing instant pop intensity so it does not look weaker. No save-compat impact.

findings.title: Enemy muzzle flash is a flat on/off pop — add a 2-3 frame additive decay + brief warm light for punch
findings.description: The enemy muzzle flash sets opacity (0.92/0.88/0.70 * scale) to a single value, then a 55ms timeout snaps it to 0 (see related finding). There is no decay curve, so enemy gunfire reads as a flat sprite blink rather than a hot flash. The infrastructure is already in place (H/V/D planes, per-shot color by shot type, scale jitter) — adding a quick per-frame opacity falloff and a sub-frame scale punch is a cheap, immediately visible upgrade to enemy gunfights, which the player sees constantly.
findings.evidence: line 12902: `e.muzzleFlashH.material.opacity=0.92*_sc;e.muzzleFlashH.scale.setScalar(_sc);` — set once, never animated; hidden by the 55ms setTimeout with no interpolation.
findings.fix: When converting to the frame-loop fade (see enemy-muzzleflash-settimeout-after-remove), ease opacity = base * (remaining/55)^1.4 each frame, and start scale at ~1.25*_sc easing down to _sc, so the flash blooms then collapses. Optionally, for the player's current target only (single enemy), add a very short-lived cheap warm flicker on the enemy's already-present accent/visor emissive (multiply by ~1.6 for one frame) to sell the shot without adding a PointLight (respecting the no-PointLight perf note at line 12890).
findings.risk: Low/visual only. Keep the additive blend and respect _trailBudget/_additiveVfxTierMul tier scaling already used for the smoke puff at 12906 so low-end tiers stay cheap.

findings.title: Dead-leader promotion can pick a `_roomFlowDormant` member, then immediately ignore the whole squad that tick
findings.description: When the leader dies, the new leader is chosen with `this.members.find(m=>!m.dead)` (line 12225), which does NOT exclude `_roomFlowDormant` members. The very next computation `aliveMembers=this.members.filter(m=>m&&!m.dead&&!m._roomFlowDormant)` (line 12241) DOES exclude dormant. If the only non-dead member is dormant, a dormant enemy becomes leader (and gets markSquadLeader's red band attached while it is supposed to be inactive), and aliveMembers is empty so update() returns early — the squad effectively orphans onto a dormant leader and stops issuing orders even though it may reactivate later, with a leader band visible on a dormant unit.
findings.fix: Make the promotion filter match the aliveMembers filter: `const alive=this.members.find(m=>!m.dead&&!m._roomFlowDormant);`. If none, return early as today. Keeps the leader band off dormant units and the leader consistent with the squad's active set.
findings.risk: Low. Only changes leader selection edge case when all non-dead members are dormant. No save-compat impact.

findings.title: A* straight-line shortcut `_navGridLineOpen` samples a thin diagonal and can cross a 1-cell-thick wall corner
findings.description: navAStar (cover-graph.js, wrapped by _navAStar at main.js 12182) short-circuits with a straight path when `_navGridLineOpen` reports clear (line 141). That check samples only `steps=max(|dx|,|dz|)` interpolated points with Math.round, so on diagonals it tests a single cell per major-axis step and can tunnel diagonally past a 1-cell-thick (0.5m) wall corner, returning a 2-point straight path that clips geometry. Enemies then walk a hair into/through a thin wall corner before the next recalc. Low visible impact because the per-enemy _tryMove collision still blocks actual penetration, but it produces brief stutter/wall-hugging at diagonal corners.
findings.evidence: lines 116-123: `const steps=Math.max(Math.abs(dx),Math.abs(dz)); ... const ix=Math.round(sx+dx*t); const iz=Math.round(sz+dz*t); if(ng.blocked[ix+iz*ng.nx])return false;` — supercover-incomplete; diagonal moves skip the off-axis neighbor cell.
findings.fix: Either bump sampling density (`steps=Math.ceil((Math.abs(dx)+Math.abs(dz)))` or sample at half-cell increments), or for diagonal steps also test the two orthogonal neighbor cells (a + b) before declaring the segment open. Lowest risk: increase steps to the Manhattan distance so each grid cell along the line is checked.
findings.risk: Low. Slightly more work in the (one-time-per-recalc) line check; could make A* fall through to full search marginally more often, which is the safe direction. No save-compat impact.
